newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says has capacity to securitise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says has capacity to securitise.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) managing director David Murray said on Wednesday the bank had the capacity to start securitising its home loan portfolio, which is Australia's biggest.
But he would not say when CBA would begin securitising mortgages or how much of its portfolio it would securitise.
"We have the capacity to do it," Murray told reporters.
"We need to be able in future, as I see the unfolding of the financial system, to offer home loans through securitisation or through the traditional bank method," Murray said.
Earlier Murray announced a cut in CBA's standard varible mortgage rate to 7.55 percent from 8.25 percent from March 27 for existing customers and from February 13 for new customers.
CBA also cut its 'no frills' Economiser variable mortgage rate to 6.95 percent from 7.35 percent.
Murray said the bank was adapting the whole structure of the group in order to find funding for home loans through securitisation.
This was to deal with the trend for savers to put their money in mutual funds rather than bank deposit accounts.

"As the financial system is evolving now, and given some of the concepts that the Wallis Inquiry have been discussing, I think it is slightly more likely that we'd finish up with a financial system that's got much more mutual fund money in it than bank money," he said, adding however that this was a big change that would take a long time.

"Conceptually one could only do mortgages through securitisation if that resulted clearly in the lowest cost to the customer on an acceptable basis to the lender of funds and to shareholders," he said.
"If necessary in concept we could do everything by securitisation if that's the best price for the customer."

Murray said it was not possible for CBA to achieve this currently because of complications with the credit code and Australian fund managers would not be able to adapt quickly enough to take on CBA's large home loan book.
